title: Comparing Audiences for a City Health Campaign · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference:
A city health team wants more people to walk to work. Last year, the team tested three campaign ideas with three different groups. The results are in the table below. Table: Campaign test results (simulated data)

| Group | Main message | People who saw the message | People who walked more |
|-------|--------------|----------------------------|------------------------|
| A: Office workers | 'Walk 20 minutes a day' | 1,000 | 250 |
| B: Parents | 'Walk your children to school' | 800 | 320 |
| C: Older adults | 'Walk with a friend' | 600 | 210 |

Group B had the highest proportion of people who walked more. In Group B, 40% of people walked more. In Group A, the figure was 25%. So the proportion in Group B was 1. 6 times as high as the proportion in Group A. Group C's proportion was 35%, which was higher than Group A's but lower than Group B's.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you often walk to work or school?
What is the best way to travel in your city?
Do you like walking with friends?
Is public transport good in your city?

Part 2
Describe a health campaign in your city. You should say: what the campaign is about; who the campaign is for; what people think of it; and explain why you think it is good or not.

Part 3
Why do some health campaigns work better for one group than another?
How can we compare the results of different campaigns?
Should governments spend money on health campaigns? Why?
What messages work well for older people?
